interactions.name: Kefka front-face enters/attacks trigger
interactions.conclusion: Whenever Kefka enters or attacks, each player discards one card during that resolving trigger. After those discards, Kefka's controller draws one card for each card type represented among cards discarded by that specific trigger. Separate Kefka triggers resolve independently and count only the cards discarded for their own resolution.

interactions.name: Harmonic Prodigy doubles both Kefka faces
interactions.conclusion: Kefka, Court Mage is a Human Wizard and Kefka, Ruler of Ruin is an Avatar Wizard. Harmonic Prodigy therefore causes triggered abilities of Kefka, as another Wizard controlled by the Prodigy's controller, to trigger an additional time. On the front this doubles each enters/attacks trigger; on the back it doubles each Ruler-of-Ruin life-loss draw trigger.

interactions.name: Ruler of Ruin transformation and life-loss engine
interactions.conclusion: Kefka's {8} ability may be activated only as a sorcery. On resolution each opponent chooses a permanent they control and the chosen permanents are sacrificed as instructed, then Kefka transforms. Once transformed, each event in which an opponent loses life during Kefka's controller's turn triggers Ruler of Ruin and draws that many cards on resolution. Combat damage and effects such as Orcish Bowmasters can therefore become card-draw events. The candidate intentionally excludes Cursed Totem because it would shut off Kefka's nonmana transform ability.

interactions.name: Anger discarded to Kefka grants same-turn haste
interactions.conclusion: Kefka's controller may discard Anger while a Kefka enters trigger resolves. Once that trigger finishes, Anger is in the graveyard. If the controller controls a land with the Mountain subtype, Anger's static ability gives Kefka haste immediately, allowing Kefka to attack that turn. The candidate contains Mountain-typed lands including Badlands, Blood Crypt, Steam Vents, and Volcanic Island.

interactions.name: Arena of Glory grants Kefka haste
interactions.conclusion: Arena of Glory's relevant mana ability can produce red mana with an additional effect that grants haste to a creature spell if that mana is spent on it. Spending that mana on the Kefka creature spell therefore lets the resulting Kefka permanent attack that turn if the spell resolves normally.

interactions.name: Gogo copying Kefka at beginning of combat
interactions.conclusion: Gogo may become a copy of another target creature its controller controls until end of turn except its name remains Gogo, Mysterious Mime. If it copies front-face Kefka, Gogo gains Kefka's attack trigger while retaining the Gogo name, so the legend rule does not remove either permanent. Gogo does not enter when it becomes a copy and therefore does not create a Kefka enters trigger. Gogo and the copied creature receive Gogo's stated power boost/haste and attack requirement, allowing both Gogo-as-Kefka and Kefka to produce attack triggers if able to attack.

interactions.name: Phantasmal Image and Phyrexian Metamorph copying Kefka
interactions.conclusion: If Phantasmal Image or Phyrexian Metamorph enters as a copy of front-face Kefka, it enters with Kefka's copiable characteristics subject to the clone's stated exceptions, so its Kefka enters ability triggers. The original and copy are legendary permanents with the same name, so the legend rule subsequently requires one to be kept, but the already-triggered enters ability remains. The deck does not rely on a single-faced clone being able to transform into Kefka's back face.

interactions.name: Saw in Half on commander Kefka
interactions.conclusion: If Saw in Half destroys Kefka and Kefka dies, Saw in Half creates two token copies as instructed. The commander did die, and a commander-zone move from the graveyard is handled at the next applicable state-based-action check after the resolving spell completes. Both legendary Kefka tokens enter during resolution and both Kefka enters abilities trigger. At the subsequent state-based-action check the legend rule leaves only one same-named Kefka token, but both already-created triggers remain and are put on the stack after state-based actions finish.

interactions.name: Molten Duplication on Kefka
interactions.conclusion: Molten Duplication creates a token copy of Kefka with the additional characteristics/effects stated by Molten Duplication, including haste and its delayed sacrifice. The token's Kefka enters ability triggers before the legend rule is checked. If the controller keeps the hasty token and puts the original legendary Kefka into the graveyard for the legend rule, that token may attack that turn and trigger Kefka's attack ability before the delayed sacrifice.

interactions.name: Essence Flux and Displacer Kitten blink Kefka
interactions.conclusion: When an effect exiles Kefka and returns that same card to the battlefield during the resolution of the same spell or ability, the return instruction occurs before state-based actions are checked. A returned front-face Kefka is a new object and produces a new enters trigger. The deck uses these cards to re-trigger Kefka, not to preserve counters or other prior-object information.

interactions.name: Tinybones and Waste Not with Kefka discard
interactions.conclusion: Kefka making opponents discard causes Tinybones, Bauble Burglar and Waste Not to trigger as applicable. Those triggers wait until the currently resolving Kefka trigger finishes before being put on the stack. Kefka still determines card types from the cards discarded for its own resolving trigger; later movement of those cards by other effects does not retroactively change that completed determination.

interactions.name: Valley Floodcaller role and limits
interactions.conclusion: Valley Floodcaller gives its controller permission to cast noncreature spells as though they had flash. Its cast trigger only pumps and untaps the creature types named in its Oracle text; it does not grant Kefka haste or untap Kefka merely because a noncreature spell was cast. The candidate does not contain the dedicated Banishing Knack/Retraction Helix bounce package and approval does not claim a Valley Floodcaller infinite loop.

interactions.name: Demonic Counsel delirium restriction
interactions.conclusion: Without delirium, Demonic Counsel searches only for a Demon card and requires the normal reveal. With four or more card types among cards in its controller's graveyard, its delirium replacement permits searching for any card instead. The candidate treats Demonic Counsel as a conditional universal tutor once delirium is established and does not misrepresent the pre-delirium mode as an unrestricted tutor.

interactions.name: Hexing Squelcher protection
interactions.conclusion: Hexing Squelcher's current Oracle text makes the relevant spells of its controller uncounterable and gives the applicable other creatures ward as stated. This can protect Kefka and proactive win attempts, but it does not stop removal or interaction that does not counter a spell or that successfully pays/avoids ward.

interactions.name: Beseech the Mirror and rejected Samut split-second anti-synergy
interactions.conclusion: A bargained Beseech the Mirror may instruct its controller to cast the qualifying exiled card without paying its mana cost during Beseech's resolution. The exact candidate does not contain Samut, Tyrant of Naktamun. This matters because giving Beseech split second while it remains on the stack during its own resolution would prevent casting another spell at that time. Samut was therefore rejected rather than accepted as generic protection.

interactions.name: Thassa's Oracle plus Demonic Consultation/Tainted Pact
interactions.conclusion: The candidate retains standard Oracle library-exile finishes. The exact candidate has 100 distinct card names, so Tainted Pact is not forced to stop by revealing a second card with the same name. Normal priority, interaction, and resolution requirements still apply.

interactions.name: Underworld Breach plus Lion's Eye Diamond plus Brain Freeze
interactions.conclusion: With sufficient graveyard material and mana, Underworld Breach permits repeated escape of Lion's Eye Diamond and Brain Freeze; LED supplies mana while Brain Freeze's storm/mill replenishes graveyard resources. The line can mill the controller's library and transition into an Oracle finish. It remains a compact secondary cEDH route rather than the commander-identity centerpiece.
